papers.title: Polar Geometry of Time-Odd EEG Dynamics
papers.summary: The paper introduces a skew-symmetric EEG state-derivative operator K and its spectral counterpart to extract time-odd, subject-discriminative longitudinal EEG features. Across four public datasets, polar orientation improved cross-session subject matching (e.g., Dortmund AUC 0.8901→0.9625, CMC@1 0.4757→0.6214), with fixed alpha-beta fusion reaching CMC@1=0.8350 and AUC=0.9855.

papers.title: An EEMD-derived slow-wave activity metric improves association with obstructive sleep apnea severity beyond conventional N3 staging.
papers.summary: Using ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) on polysomnography EEG from 823 Sleep Heart Health Study participants, the authors derived a slow-wave activity (SWA)-based slow-wave sleep (SWS) metric and tested its association with obstructive sleep apnea severity. EEMD-derived SWS correlated more strongly with apnea-hypopnea index (coefficients -0.36 to -0.39) than conventional N3 staging (-0.27 to -0.28), with stronger associations in high-risk heart rate or hypoxia strata.

papers.title: States of dynamic connectivity flow in temporal multiplex networks: A case study in human epilepsy and postictal aphasia.
papers.summary: The authors present a temporal multiplex network framework for multifrequency dynamic functional connectivity that characterizes instantaneous reconfiguration speed and modular reorganization, applied to stereo-EEG from epilepsy patients. Seizure onset was linked to slowed dFC speed, and a postictal regime of low speed and frozen allegiance aligned most strongly with clinician-annotated aphasia.

papers.title: When More Is Not Better: Component Anti-Synergy in a P300 Speller
papers.summary: The paper tested whether combining individually promising components in a P300 speller is additive using a four-component full-factorial experiment varying Euclidean Alignment, xDAWN spatial filtering, subject calibration, and language model priors on a public dataset. Results showed that component value is conditional rather than additive, with calibration the strongest singular contributor, anti-synergy between components, and language model support not universally beneficial.

papers.title: Target-Session early stopping for cross-session EEG mental workload classification: a reusable deployment-oriented method.
papers.summary: The paper describes Target-Session Early Stopping (TSES), which replaces within-session validation for early stopping with 50 labeled epochs from the target session to improve cross-session EEG mental workload classification. TSES improved accuracy on all 14 directional transfer pairs and was more data-efficient than calibration fine-tuning; with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift screen, the protocol requires about four minutes of target-session recording.

papers.title: pyAvalanches: A Python Package for Analyzing Spatiotemporal Propagation in Neuronal Avalanches
papers.summary: The paper introduces pyAvalanches, an open-source Python package providing a standardized end-to-end pipeline for neuronal avalanche analysis from electrophysiological recordings, with core innovation in computing Avalanche Transition Matrices to map spatiotemporal propagation patterns and derive network-based metrics. It demonstrates utility through group-level analysis of a public resting-state EEG dataset comparing propagation patterns across clinical populations.

papers.title: Active Bed Microclimate Regulation Modulates Sleep Architecture, Autonomic, and Central Nervous System Activity during Sleep
papers.summary: In 18 adults undergoing two overnight polysomnography sessions, active bed microclimate heating and cooling across six temperature settings modulated sleep architecture, autonomic activity, and cortical EEG activity. All active settings increased slow-wave sleep odds (OR 1.21–3.65, largest for high cooling), heating accelerated early sleep deepening, and cooling produced graded heart-rate reductions, suggesting nonlinear thermal sweet spots.

papers.title: A confidence-gated source selection strategy for cross-session transfer in brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: Developed confidence-gated selective-transfer pipelines (Minimum-Distance Multi-Source and Bridge Domain) for cross-session motor imagery EEG decoding and benchmarked them against uniform-pooling and distance-weighted-pooling baselines on two public datasets. The Bridge Domain Pipeline achieved top accuracy levels while requiring substantially reduced execution time and fewer source sessions, indicating that how retained sessions are integrated matters more than session selection alone.

papers.title: Investigating the influence of anti-seizure medications on aperiodic EEG activity.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Examined effects of lamotrigine (300 mg), levetiracetam (3000 mg), and placebo on periodic and aperiodic resting EEG parameters in 13 healthy male volunteers. Lamotrigine reduced aperiodic offset and exponent and levetiracetam reduced exponent in the eyes-open condition, with both drugs also altering periodic theta, alpha, beta, and gamma power, suggesting aperiodic EEG measures can characterize antiseizure medication effects.

papers.title: Delta rhythm and voice familiarity organize neural entrainment in the infant brain
papers.summary: Used high-density EEG to test neural entrainment in thirty 6-month-old infants listening to vocally rhythmic syllables from their mother or a stranger at delta (2 Hz) and theta (4 Hz) rates. Found frequency-specific delta entrainment over frontal and temporal clusters, with left temporal cortex selectively entraining to the mother's voice and right frontal cortex to the stranger's voice, indicating experience-dependent hemispheric organization of temporal prediction.

papers.title: NeuroStream: spectral-spatio-temporal deep learning for visual stimulus classification from EEG.
papers.summary: Introduced a Spectral-Spatio-Temporal representation that converts raw EEG into a video-like format using wavelet transforms and electrode-position mapping, and a lightweight deep learning framework (NeuroStream-SST) for visual stimulus classification. On EEGCVPR40, the approach reached top accuracy in the high-gamma band under standard splits, and additional protocols showed accuracy declined as label-session association weakened, highlighting temporal-correlation confounds.

papers.title: Behavioral and autonomic manifestations of suspected focal impaired awareness seizures supported by interictal electroencephalographic findings in three dogs: a case series.
papers.summary: Described three dogs with recurrent behavioral and autonomic episodes (fear, restlessness, hypersalivation, staring) and no motor signs, in which 1.5-4 h EEG monitoring revealed epileptiform discharges predominantly in parietal and temporal regions. Antiseizure medication reduced episode frequency and intensity, with complete seizure freedom in two dogs, supporting EEG as an adjunct for recognizing suspected focal impaired awareness seizures in dogs.

papers.title: During natural vision, semantic novelty modulates fixation-related processing in primate cortex
papers.summary: Fixation-related potentials and intracranial high-frequency activity were recorded in humans and macaques during natural movie viewing to test whether semantic novelty across saccades modulates visual processing. Only semantic novelty, not low- or mid-level novelty, modulated frontal and occipital fixation-related potentials in scalp EEG and broadband high-frequency activity in ventral visual and frontal areas, with stronger effects for movies than static images and early frontal modulation suggesting top-down integration.

papers.title: Chronotype-specific associations of sleep-wake schedule with behavioral, physiological, and psychological parameters.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This study compared sleep-wake schedules aligned with individual chronotype (Self-Time) versus social clock time (Clock-Time) and measured subjective states, sleep pressure via EEG, and motor/cognitive performance at 1.5 and 12.5 hours post-awakening. Early chronotypes showed typical sleep pressure accumulation with time awake, while late chronotypes were more affected by sleep timing and had atypical sleep pressure patterns; motor ability improved in the afternoon for both chronotypes regardless of schedule, but cognitive performance peaked earlier for early chronotypes and later for late chronotypes independent of time of day.

papers.title: Uncovering the representational geometry of durations
papers.summary: Using behavioural similarity judgments and EEG oddball detection, the authors constructed representational dissimilarity matrices and found that duration representation is best explained by three latent dimensions (magnitude, contextual encoding, periodic component) consistent with a generalized helical model, with neural geometry showing logarithmic encoding around 150 ms and spring-like geometry around 300 ms after offset.

papers.title: Electrical bioimpedance spectral markers distinguish balance ability in older adults without provoking fall risk.
papers.summary: The study investigated whether spectral features of electrical bioimpedance (EBI) recorded over the extensor digitorum longus during safe static postures can distinguish balance ability in older adults without provoking falls. In 28 adults aged 60–74 stratified by single-leg stance performance, better balance was associated with stronger oscillatory organization of the EBI signal (greater power concentration in identifiable spectral peaks and a greater peak count), while poorer balance showed a more broadband profile with larger irregular low-frequency fluctuations; after correction, two frequency-domain features remained significant.

papers.title: Excitation/inhibition balance subtypes in autism and their genetic, neural, and clinical profiles.
papers.summary: Using resting-state EEG in 310 youths (164 with autism, 146 typically developing), the study derived excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance measures and identified three neural subgroups within the autistic cohort: typical E/I, E > I, and E < I. The E/I imbalance subgroups had altered clinical phenotypes and distinct genetic profiles, with genes in identified CNVs showing more prenatal expression in the E < I subgroup and more postnatal expression in the E > I subgroup, suggesting clinically meaningful neural and genetic subtypes.

papers.title: Sources of the N15 TMS-evoked potential following motor cortex stimulation localize rostrals to TMS-induced electric fields and depend on dose.
papers.summary: The study characterized the source activity of the N15 TMS-evoked potential relative to TMS-induced electric fields (E-fields) in 16 healthy adults who received TMS-EEG over the left motor hand area at six intensities during rest and tonic contraction. The N15 source was consistently located rostral to the peak E-field, with the spatial disparity decreasing as stimulation dose increased; source activity clustered in left premotor and primary motor cortex, suggesting transsynaptic propagation via cortico-cortical or cortico-subcortico-cortical pathways.

papers.title: A multimodal EEG-based psychological risk representation method using spatiotemporal graph attention and adaptive gated fusion.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal EEG-based method for psychological risk representation that combines spatiotemporal graph attention networks, bidirectional LSTM for temporal dynamics, and adaptive gated fusion to integrate static psychological features with dynamic EEG signals. On the AMIGOS dataset, the method significantly improved risk prediction accuracy and robustness over questionnaire-based assessment and revealed key EEG features through attention weight analysis, supporting interpretable multimodal mental health assessment.

papers.title: Visual speech enhances phoneme separability in human superior temporal gyrus
papers.summary: Using intracranial EEG in 12 epilepsy patients performing an audiovisual speech task, the study found that congruent visual speech improved word and phoneme decoding accuracy and classifier confidence in superior temporal gyrus, with earlier decoding for audiovisual than auditory-only speech and effects primarily for onset consonants rather than rimes. The authors conclude that visual speech sharpens categorical phoneme representations in STG.

papers.title: Enhancement of Vagal Tone, Cognitive Processing, and Self-Regulation Through Short-Term Audible Mantram Repetition Practice in Novice Meditators.
papers.summary: This randomized three-group study in 39 novice meditators found that 4 weeks of daily audible Hare Krishna Mantram repetition significantly improved heart rate variability, P300 latency and amplitude, Stroop reaction times, and self-regulation scores, while sham and silent practice showed limited cognitive/self-regulation effects. The authors conclude that audible mantram repetition may be a promising non-pharmacological approach for chronic stress, autonomic balance, and executive function.

papers.title: TMS-EEG Correlate of Suicidal Ideation in Individuals with Depression: A Multi-Site Synthesis.
papers.summary: In a multi-site synthesis of cross-sectional TMS-EEG data from 299 adults with major depressive disorder and inadequate antidepressant response, more negative N100 peak amplitude in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex was significantly associated with greater suicidal ideation severity (OR=1.52, p=0.002), independent of age, sex, depression severity, and site. No significant association was found for global mean field amplitude AUC.

papers.title: Mentally transformed representations in memory are linked to their originals
papers.summary: Using multivariate EEG decoding during a mental rotation and retro-cue working memory task, the study found that an original orientation representation remained decodable after mental rotation and after encoding an additional item, but its retention depended on attentional selection of the rotation product: original and rotation product were retained or dropped together. The authors propose that mental transformation creates a dependent representational link between the product and its source representation.

papers.title: Emotion regulation difficulties are differentially associated with late positive potential during the processing and regulation of social-affective stimuli.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: In 79 adults performing an emotion regulation task with EEG, greater Lack of Emotional Control was uniquely associated with larger late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes across conditions, while greater Lack of Emotional Awareness was associated with smaller LPP amplitudes and a more negative LPP during expressive suppression.

papers.title: Bridging Temporal and Spatial Scales: Contemporary Advances in EEG-fMRI Integration With a Focus on Epilepsy.
papers.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent methodological, acquisition, and analytical developments in EEG-fMRI integration for epilepsy research, highlighting how combining high temporal and spatial resolution can improve characterization of epileptogenic networks and support presurgical evaluation. It also outlines remaining technical, analytical, and translational challenges to broader clinical adoption.

papers.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Studied differential privacy (DP) for clinical EEG feature anonymization using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations across client-side, centralized, and decentralized deployment scenarios. Found that the choice of mechanism, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly influenced data utility, highlighting a practical privacy-utility trade-off in small, imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Distinct neural routes for evaluative and informational social influence.
papers.summary: A preregistered EEG study (n=87) using the Judge-Advisor System found that feedback elicited a feedback-related negativity that decreased with confidence, whereas advice produced sustained late positive complex activity whose onset slowed with higher confidence and lower proximity, dissociating evaluative and informational social influence.

papers.title: Development and temporal validation of a postoperative nomogram based on clinical, surgical, histopathological, and semi-quantitative EEG features for predicting seizure-free survival in children after focal epilepsy surgery.
papers.summary: In a single-center retrospective cohort of 256 children who underwent focal epilepsy surgery, a nomogram incorporating longer epilepsy duration, absence of definitive MRI lesion, histopathological diagnosis, subtotal resection, and high NREM interictal spike index (>38 spikes/h) achieved optimism-corrected C-indices of 0.81 in training and 0.79 in temporal validation for predicting 1- and 2-year seizure-free survival.

papers.title: A unified machine learning framework for oral cancer classification using Raman spectra from tissue, serum, and urine.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.summary: A unified machine learning framework using Raman spectra from tissue, serum, and urine classified oral cancer with AUCs of 0.905 for MLP, 0.964 for SVM, and 0.948 for RF under patient-level group K-fold cross-validation, showing that a single domain-conditioned architecture can learn cancer-associated spectral representations that transfer across biosample types.

papers.title: Effects of multiple object tracking training on visual attention and sports decision-making in novice female basketball players: evidence from EyeLink-EEG synchronization.
papers.summary: In 56 novice female basketball players, nine weeks of multiple-object tracking training significantly improved sports decision-making accuracy and increased fixation on key and related areas, with decreased N1, P1, and LPC and increased LNC ERP components during decision-making.

papers.title: BIS Versus End-tidal Anaesthetic Gas Concentration-guided General Anaesthesia for Prevention of Intraoperative Awareness in Elective Surgery: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial compared BIS-guided and end-tidal anesthetic gas concentration-guided general anesthesia for preventing intraoperative awareness in 674 elective surgery patients and found no significant difference in awareness incidence between groups.

papers.title: Phenylbutyrate-Responsive SLC6A1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder Associated With a Familial Variant.
papers.summary: This case report describes a three-generation family with a heterozygous SLC6A1 variant segregating with neurodevelopmental and epileptic phenotypes; treatment with glycerol phenylbutyrate produced complete seizure freedom and reduced epileptiform discharges in the proband.

papers.title: A systematic approach to MR spectroscopy of the brain: Indications, protocol, metabolites, and spectral analysis in neurologic diseases.
papers.summary: This review provides a systematic approach to brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy, covering indications, acquisition protocols, metabolite interpretation, and characteristic metabolic patterns across neurological diseases to aid differential diagnosis.

papers.title: Nucleic Acid Turnover and Lipid Remodeling Distinguish T Cell Activation and Exhaustion States via Label-Free Raman Spectroscopy.
papers.summary: This study introduces label-free Raman spectroscopy combined with a 1-D convolutional neural network to distinguish T cell activation and exhaustion states, achieving >97% accuracy and identifying nucleic acid and lipid alterations as key spectral features.

papers.title: Transcranial Doppler Ultrasonography as a Complementary Exam in Brain Death Determination: Impact on Protocol Duration and ICU Length of Stay-A Single-Center Study in Brazil.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study of 178 brain death protocols in a Brazilian ICU found that transcranial Doppler ultrasonography use was independently associated with a 53.9% reduction in median protocol duration and shorter post-protocol ICU length of stay, without significant difference in organ donation rates.

papers.title: Evaluating and comparing the signalling and functional landscape of hiPSC-CMs derived from patients with dilated cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: Generated hiPSC-CMs from two healthy controls and two dilated cardiomyopathy patients and profiled patient-specific GPCR signaling using PKA and ERK biosensors plus calcium handling, contractility, and electrophysiology. The pipeline revealed altered molecular signaling and functional signatures in DCM lines, providing a platform for personalized mechanism discovery and treatment development.

papers.title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational study protocol aims to investigate spatiotemporal brain responses to visual food cues using electroencephalography and behavioral responses using a gamified smartphone Go/NoGo task in 94 pregnant individuals at 12-16 and 31-36 weeks of gestation. The study will examine associations with metabolic, psychological, and behavioral outcomes to understand excessive gestational weight gain.

papers.title: Recurrent Catatonia During Longitudinal Evaluation of Possible Seronegative Autoimmune Encephalitis: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a woman in her early 20s with recurrent catatonia during longitudinal evaluation of possible seronegative autoimmune encephalitis, with symptoms improving after lorazepam and prior response to electroconvulsive therapy. The case highlights the value of syndromic reassessment and timely catatonia treatment despite etiologic uncertainty.

papers.title: A Reassessment of Prophylactic Antibiotics in Low-Infection-Risk Electrophysiology Procedures.
papers.summary: This review evaluates the practice of prophylactic antibiotic administration and infection rates in low-infection-risk electrophysiology procedures, finding that periprocedural infection rates are low regardless of antibiotic use. Existing studies are insufficient to determine benefit of routine antibiotics, and adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed.

papers.title: Predictors of seizures after endovascular aneurysm exclusion: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of six studies found that hydrocephalus (OR 3.91, 95% CI: 1.22-12.53), Fisher grade 3+4 blood distribution (OR 3.29, 95% CI: 1.55-6.97, I2=0%), Hunt-Hess grade 1-3 (OR 3.15, 95% CI: 1.73-5.72), and WFNS grade 4-5 (OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.14-3.02) were associated with higher likelihood of post-endovascular aneurysm exclusion seizures, while age, sex, MCA involvement, and cerebral oedema were not significant. Evidence is limited by observational designs and heterogeneous seizure definitions.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
